Foregrounding Care: Recognizing Moments of Activation and Utilizing Self-Regulation Strategies
sessionabstract: We are all managing a lot these days, both in our work and in our personal lives, and it is easy to feel overwhelmed. The implications of this show up in many ways in the classroom and workplace. Our students often struggle with executive functioning, are experiencing increasing levels of anxiety, and are coping with other mental health symptoms that can, at times, feel incapacitating. Our colleagues are navigating competing demands on their time, and feeling overextended can be emotionally taxing in ways that can cause both tension and conflict. This session will invite us to explore moments when the behaviors we are observing—or experiencing ourselves—are the result of feeling activated. We will consider the impact of these moments, for the individual feeling activated, for those present in the classroom or workplace, and for our roles as educators, advisors, coaches, colleagues, or supervisors. This session will offer concrete strategies that can be used both during moments when individuals are feeling activated and as regular practices that help support self-regulation.

The dynamics of campus leadership are constantly evolving. Concepts like "crunch," "hustle," and "work families" are giving way to a greater emphasis on self-care and work-life balance. The era of the loudest voice in the room prevailing is fading; now is the time for empathetic leadership.
Empathetic leaders prioritize understanding others—their perspectives, motivations, and experiences. They actively seek to connect with the people around them and adapt their leadership style to meet different needs.

"Empathetic leaders take a genuine interest in the people around them—what makes them tick, what inspires them, and how they feel. They want to understand why people are the way they are, and this desire helps them connect with many types of people and adapt their style depending on who they are interacting with."
— Tony Robbins

Over the years, I have focused on developing leadership approaches rooted in empathy as a core tenet. I invite you to join an open discussion on the strengths and challenges of leading large, multi-generational teams through this lens.

sessionTitle: Faculty & Staff Guide to Reciprocal Wellness - Supporting Our Students, Supporting Ourselves
sessionabstract: Introduction: who we are; where to find us; when students should be referred for counseling; the referral process; steps to engaging in counseling; confidentiality; cost and resources available to students. The aim of our counseling center is to support students with mental health concerns. The goal of this presentation is to look at wellness as reciprocal. How well you do in supporting your students is affected by how well you are doing. We will look at the importance of recognizing the interconnection between cultivating wellness in our students and in ourselves. By paying closer attention to shifts in your baseline you will be better attuned to students who are struggling. Self-awareness is the first step to better self-care. Noticing the early signs that you are stressed or overwhelmed can help you intervene before things become unmanageable. We will help you identify what leads you to feeling overwhelmed and stressed and what helps you to feel calm and relaxed. Self-care doesn't have to be relegated to the end of the workday. We will look at how you can integrate better self-care into your workday to support yourself and your students.

sessionTitle: "Be the Professor You Needed": Intentional Course Design for Empathy & Care
sessionabstract:
What does it actually mean to create a classroom where students feel safe enough to learn? Not the compliance version — the accessibility statement buried in your syllabus, the land acknowledgment you read once — but the kind of care that shapes how you design every policy, every assignment, every interaction from day one.

This workshop invites faculty to reflect on what empathetic teaching looks like in practice: building structures where students don't have to "trauma dump" to get an extension, where showing up matters more than performing, and where your policies say I am on your team before a student ever has to ask. We'll explore practical strategies for humanizing your classroom — from syllabus language to day-one framing — grounded in the belief that education should be dignity-affirming and psychologically safe for everyone in the room, including you.

Leave with language, examples, and a framework you can use this semester.
Learn ways to take movement breaks at your desk. Be prepared to move.

sessionTitle: Kindling Connections: Building mentoring relationships based on wisdom sharing, reciprocity and growth
sessionabstract: The Multicultural Life and Diversity Office staff will facilitate a workshop talking about informal and formal mentoring relationships between students and colleagues. We will discuss the benefits of mentoring, personal experiences, and best practices. Participants will explore how meaningful mentoring relationships can support personal growth, academic success, career development, and a sense of belonging. Through this workshop attendees will learn strategies for building authentic connections and will also highlight the importance of building relationships with and creating supportive environments for individuals from diverse backgrounds. Our workshop will provide opportunities for interactive activities and discussion about mentoring relationships.

sessionTitle: Teaching with Teams: Using TEAMS to teach online classes

sessionabstract: Academic and professional faculty face many challenges in balancing commitments that can come in the form of both obligations and opportunities. How do you decide what you commit to without falling into a vortex of poor work/life balance or burnout? In this presentation we will consider some ideologies underpinning what it might mean for you to feel "balanced," some considerations for career stages, and concrete actions to promote "joy" and well-being in your position. This session will involve an interactive presentation, workshop, and attention to joy and play!
